documents.abstract: The article examines India’s 2026 amendments to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules in relation to synthetically generated information, covering deepfake creation and distribution. It first identifies the need for regulation in India, drawing on recent instances of deepfake-related events, and then places those needs in a comparative perspective by analysing regulatory approaches in China, the European Union and the United States. The article argues that India has adopted a hybrid intermediary-liability model that combines labelling, provenance, technical-prevention, user-declaration and accelerated takedown obligations while still relying on existing criminal, electoral, consumer-protection, privacy and personality-rights frameworks to do much of the hard work. By situating India’s framework within the broader global regulatory environment, the article contributes to current debates on how legal systems should respond to harmful synthetic media without unduly constraining other beneficial uses of generative AI. Overall, the analysis shows that India’s Intermediary Guidelines Amendments offer a reasonable response to the main issues at stake but leave considerable room for other areas of law to do the heavy lifting. The article concludes on a cautionary note, highlighting the expected challenges of future implementation.

We discuss an effective paradigm of utilizing AI agents to better compile quantum circuits when one can constrain bottleneck subroutines to have some form of classically verifiable structure. For example, when critical subroutines are composed exclusively of reversible classical logic, phasing operations, and measurement based uncomputation, one can efficiently simulate execution for classical inputs. This property facilitates efficient certification of approximate circuit synthesis via a form of fuzz testing, provided suitable assumptions on the input distribution. While this pattern was recently exploited to improve quantum cryptanalysis circuits, here we highlight the flexibility of the broader approach by discussing three important applications. (1) The computation of $1/\sqrt{x}$ that bottlenecks real space simulations of the Coulomb operator such as those important for modeling inertial confinement fusion reactors. (2) The decoding of Reed-Solomon codes which bottlenecks the decoded quantum interferometry algorithm when used to approximately solve the optimal polynomial intersection problem. And (3) the quantum look-up tables and controlled application of Givens rotations that bottleneck the most performant quantum algorithms for simulating chemistry in second quantization. We discuss reference implementations of these algorithms and how they can be constrained and verified in the interest of seeding a Kaggle competition designed to accelerate AI-based research into the optimization of their compilation.

Large Language Models (LLMs) have greatly assisted legal professionals. However, our empirical studies reveal that, when faced with underspecified consultations from non-experts, current LLMs often produce irresponsible responses with limited utility despite lacking sufficient case details for definitive conclusions. To better assist laypeople, legal LLMs must identify focal points of dispute and proactively elicit crucial context from users. Unfortunately, existing data resources often focus on interaction and response quality, offering limited insight into how proactive interaction affects LLMs' downstream claim-level judgment prediction in actual civil cases. To address this gap, we introduce \textbf{LexPilot}, a benchmark linking proactive legal interaction to claim-level verdict prediction using authentic Chinese civil judgments. Constructed from 432 real-world judgments across 36 common causes of action, LexPilot comprises expert-reviewed pairs of complete and underspecified consultation histories with corresponding court verdicts. Experiments reveal that current LLMs struggle with proactive legal interactions in underspecified consultations, with downstream judgment prediction substantially underperforming that in the fully specified consultation setup (-23.84% on average). Further analysis identifies critical bottlenecks hindering these capabilities. Our work highlights the urgent need for more user-centered legal AI to better serve the public.

Artificial intelligence is increasingly deployed through systems in which authority, execution, oversight, and consequence no longer belong to the same actor. A model may be developed by one organization, integrated by another, configured by an enterprise, instructed by a human, executed through an AI agent, routed through external tools, and experienced by a person who had no role in any of those decisions. The resulting liability problem is not adequately described by asking whether a human remained "in the loop" or whether an audit trail exists. This working paper develops the GAILC Authority Boundary framework. It defines the Authority Boundary as the point at which consequential decision rights, discretion, intervention responsibility, or consequence-bearing responsibility passes from one actor, system, organization, or layer to another, and analyses each boundary through five elements: Authority, Transfer, Reliance, Intervention, and Consequence. The framework identifies two difficult liability cases that conventional control models often leave unresolved. Intended-Execution Liability concerns harm produced when a system remains within its authority, follows policy, uses permitted tools, and operates substantially as designed. No-Action Liability concerns harm produced or worsened where an actor bears an identifiable duty or assigned responsibility to act, possesses the authority, information, timing, and practical capacity to do so, yet no consequential intervention occurs. The paper introduces the Authority Envelope, the distinction between authorization and judgment, the Silence-as-Authority Problem, the GAILC Allocation Test, Consequence Ownership, Allocation Completeness and Allocation Adequacy, Residual Consequence, and Orphaned Harm. It proposes a standardized Authority Boundary Record (ABR) designed to support verification, contestability, and independent adjudication, together with a boundary failure taxonomy, an irreversibility threshold, an inter-organizational allocation procedure, and a pre-deployment test. Its central proposition is that traceability is evidence, not allocation: an authority and execution chain may be fully reconstructable while accountability and consequence allocation remain incomplete. The framework is analytical and does not determine legal liability. It is positioned in relation to agency law, duties concerning failures to act, design-defect analysis, and scholarship on the problem of many hands, responsibility gaps, and moral crumple zones. This paper is the third in the GAILC Working Paper series, following WP001 (The Human Presence Economy) and WP002 (The Intervention Test).
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract Welding efficiency and environmental performance are critical in industrial applications. This study presents a cradle to gate life cycle assessment (LCA) comparing conventional tungsten inert gas (TIG) welding with activated tungsten inert gas (A-TIG) welding for producing 100 mm bead-on-plate welds on grade 304L stainless steel. In A TIG, a TiO₂ methanol flux allows a lower welding current while achieving a comparable penetration depth. Calculated welding electricity consumption, measured flux-preparation electricity consumption, and material inputs were modeled in SimaPro 9.2 using Ecoinvent 3 datasets. Midpoint impacts were assessed using the EPD 2018 method, and endpoint impacts were assessed using ReCiPe 2016 Hierarchist method. Results show that A-TIG reduced welding electricity consumption by approximately 40% compared with TIG and yielded lower modeled acidification, eutrophication, and global warming potentials. Water scarcity impacts were nearly identical for the two processes. However, However, A-TIG’s normalized photochemical ozone creation potential (POCP) score was 68.1 percentage points higher than TIG’s, with the higher impact set to 100% in each category, primarily because of modeled methanol emissions and upstream flux-production impacts. A one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis covering 30 scenarios showed that the comparative ranking of the two processes remained unchanged within the investigated parameter ranges, with methanol mass identified as the dominant influence on POCP. Endpoint modeling indicated that the human-health category dominated the weighted damage profile. These results represent potential life-cycle impacts rather than measured occupational health effects. This experimental cradle-to-gate LCA of penetration-matched bead-on-plate welding indicates that flux-assisted welding can reduce several impacts associated with electricity consumption while introducing trade-offs related to photochemical ozone creation. These findings support the optimization of activating flux formulations and welding parameters within the investigated conditions, while their applicability to industrial joints requires further validation.

General Background The pre-analytical stage represents a critical phase within clinical laboratory testing sequences because it involves initial procedures largely reliant on manual handling and personnel precision. Specific Background Implementation of Internal Quality Improvement (IQI) serves as the primary evaluation tool to analyze pre-analytical factors affecting clinical laboratory test results. Knowledge Gap Although overall pre-analytical quality appears optimal, recurring human-factor errors during critical operational points remain inadequately mitigated across routine workflows. Aims This study evaluates pre-analytical variables influencing laboratory test accuracy and assesses the role of educational interventions in mitigating human-induced errors. Results Findings indicate that while internal quality performance generally ranges from good to very good, critical vulnerabilities persist during patient identification, phlebotomy execution, and anticoagulant-to-specimen volume ratios. Novelty This literature review synthesizes multi-year publication data from 2015 to 2015 to map recurrent pre-analytical discrepancies and evaluate targeted educational impacts. Implications Systematic staff education and standardized compliance significantly enhance procedural reliability and clinical diagnostic safety. Key Findings Highlights Pre-analytical error rates are predominantly driven by manual handling vulnerabilities during patient identification and sample collection, Phlebotomy technique discrepancies and sample-to-anticoagulant ratio deviations significantly compromise test result accuracy, Structured educational interventions effectively improve staff compliance and reduce human-factor errors. Keywords Pre-Analytical, Internal Quality Improvement, Clinical Laboratory, Laboratory Errors, Quality Control
topics: Clinical Laboratory Practices and Quality Control

documents.abstract: Arguments that AI systems will evolve in harmful ways are largely made in the abstract. We provide a concrete empirical example. We simulate simple markets consisting of populations of twenty Large Language Model agents tasked with solving arithmetic problems. Agents differ only in their system prompt; those that go bankrupt are removed and replaced by mutated copies of the prompts of successful agents. Two market conditions select for opposite phenotypes: a market that rewards accuracy produces agents with high accuracy (94%) and high token use; a market that charges per token produces agents with low accuracy (10%) and low token use. In the second market, only tokens are incentivised yet we see a collapse in accuracy. Token use and accuracy are correlated traits such that selection on one also moves the other, and behaviour adapts along an unpriced dimension. A third neutral condition with no selection allows us to separate these effects from bias in the mutation operator. Adaptation occurs through a collective optimisation process that operates above the level of individual agents, who are never told the payment rule, do not receive feedback, and have no memory.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Wireless Digital Twins are emerging as a key enabler for predictive network control in 6G Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) systems. However, closed-loop V2I DTs face two dual-stage communication bottlenecks arising from model parameter exchange for V2I DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic delivery after each reconstruction. This paper proposes a closed-loop dual-stage End-to-End (E2E) latency optimization framework that integrates Compressed Personalized Federated Learning with a unified Large-Language-Model-guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning approach. A CPFL-enabled decision-oriented V2I DT is first constructed by jointly predicting Path Loss (PL) and Quality-of-Experience (QoE)-oriented Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Then the framework comprises two temporally coupled but latency-wise distinct optimization stages: Stage I minimizes the joint Uplink (UL) and Downlink (DL) E2E transmission latency of compressed shared backbone's parameters, and Stage II minimizes the service-aware E2E latency of multi-service V2I traffic. As the two stages share aligned agent roles and action space, we develop a unified Semantic-Aware Guidance-Enhanced Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization framework, in which the LLM acts as a training-time semantic planner that provides high-level traffic splitting and power allocation guidance to reduce inefficient exploration, while the MARL agents execute feasible low-level actions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables efficient V2I DT reconstruction and significantly reduces both E2E latency for DT reconstruction and multi-service V2I traffic. The proposed SAGE-MAPPO supports cross-stage policy reuse by sequentially solving the two stages within each DT update cycle, which accelerates convergence relative to the existing baselines and facilitates timely DT updates in dynamic V2I scenarios.

Local learning algorithms can reshape resource requirements of artificial intelligence. The memory bottleneck of standard end-to-end backpropagation lies in the need to store all network activations until the loss gradient has been propagated back through. Local learning avoids this, but typically at a cost in accuracy. We study how to achieve accurate and memory efficient local learning in transformers. For each transformer block, we train a local proxy network to predict the global network output via distillation. Gradients can be independently propagated through this local proxy while estimating well the backpropagation gradients. In theory, this approach is exact for deep linear networks; in non-linear residual models, the gradient error can be bounded when using the appropriate residual proxy. We verify this numerically and demonstrate that optimizing the distillation loss improves gradient estimation. Evaluating the performance of proxy propagation on CIFAR-100 in vision transformers, we find that it achieves a better accuracy/memory trade-off compared to other local algorithms. Finally, we show that the method is further relevant for fine-tuning large language models on a small memory budget. Our method trains faster and achieves higher performance than memory-efficient zeroth-order learning algorithms with comparable memory cost.

Locally deployed large language models (LLMs) can reduce reliance on remote cloud services for natural language smart building automation, but backend-facing processing requires correct outcome selection, alignment with local capabilities, and valid structured outputs. We investigate whether a complete outcome-specific prompting design improves compact-model outputs beyond generic route-then-generate prompting. The proposed LocalIntent approach routes requests to ordinary or persistent-rule branches: the former produces commands, clarifications, or rejections, while the latter generates trigger-action rules, followed by deterministic validation. We evaluate four locally executed Gemma and Qwen models spanning 2B-9B parameters on 101 non-persistent and 54 persistent-rule records, comparing Monolithic prompting, generic two-stage prompting, LocalIntent, and validation-guided repair. Across the evaluated datasets, LocalIntent achieves higher intent understanding, device identification, and action/parameter correctness than generic two-stage prompting, while clarification/mode correctness remains model-dependent. The largest gains occur for rules, where LocalIntent improves intent understanding from 26.4% to 80.6%, device identification from 59.3% to 84.7%, rule-mode correctness from 49.1% to 98.6%, and action/parameter correctness from 5.6% to 44.9%. For non-persistent requests, pooled gains are smaller: intent understanding increases from 39.6% to 53.2%, and action/parameter correctness from 30.7% to 42.8%.

LLM agents are widely used for software development and debugging, but their adoption in embedded systems, especially for wireless tasks, remains limited. This is because embedded development requires hardware-in-the-loop testing. Agents cannot directly observe the spectrum, probe pins, or measure power, so they cannot verify wireless link functionality; currently, human engineers perform this verification. We systematically evaluate whether LLM agents can establish wireless links when provided with hardware access. We introduce LoopHIL, a framework that lets agents control a multi-device RF bench, monitor it with a spectrum analyzer, logic analyzer, and energy meter, and validate links against a verification ladder, all within code-enforced safety limits. Across four increasingly complex tasks, from generating a carrier to backscatter decoding by a commercial receiver, and using six models from two vendors, hardware-in-the-loop increases task completion rates from 54% to 79% and from 17% to 83% on the most challenging task. It also halves task time and output tokens. With debugging tools, agents decrease tag power consumption by up to 96%. However, small models often report unverified claims, so independent hardware checks remain necessary.

This study examines TikTok video content and comment sections during the 2025 German federal election campaign. We conceptualize comment sections as affective publics: networked arenas in which users enact publicness through affirmation, opposition, and emotional expression. Empirically, the analysis draws on 12,685 videos from 1,274 political accounts, engagement metrics, and almost two million comments, examined through LLM-based topic classification and automated stance and emotion classification. Methodologically, the study shows how LLM-assisted analysis can move beyond content classification to trace how political messages are taken up, emotionally charged, and redirected in audience interaction. Results show that campaign-focused content dominates political TikTok, followed by more substantive debate about economic issues, democracy and its institutions, social policy, and migration. Yet visibility of this content and audience responses vary sharply across parties. The AfD combines high posting frequency with strongly supportive and emotionally aligned comment environments, while centrist and governing parties face predominantly critical or mocking responses. Cross-party hostility analysis further reveals asymmetric patterns of animosity, with negative engagement directed toward specific political opponents rather than distributed randomly. The study shows that TikTok functions simultaneously as a space of participatory visibility and affective polarization. Conceptually, it extends the study of affective publics to platformed campaign communication, showing how emotional alignment and antagonism organize visibility and engagement on TikTok.

The growing diversity of wireless services in sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication systems calls for reusable channel representations that support multiple tasks across different propagation environments. However, deploying such representations between user equipment and the base station in frequency-division duplexing systems faces uplink feedback constraints. This paper proposes a distributed framework based on an angle-delay-domain large wireless model (LWMa) for multiple tasks. LWMa exploits angle-delay structure and delay truncation to improve feature extraction and reduce computational cost. A scenario-specific network inspired by Perceiver IO (input-output) compresses embeddings for channel reconstruction tasks, while other tasks use a low-dimensional compact global embedding. Embedding reconstruction training followed by channel-quality-guided fine-tuning preserves information useful for downstream processing. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method supports effective channel reconstruction and multiple tasks under limited feedback with reduced deployment complexity. Further evaluations show that the recovered embeddings generalize to additional tasks and support split inference.

The integration of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) into pharmaceutical sciences is reshaping the development of advanced drug delivery systems. Traditional gastroprotective drug delivery systems (GRDDS) are designed to prolong the residence time of oral dosage forms in the stomach to enhance bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy for drugs with narrow absorption windows. However, conventional formulation development often relies on empirical optimization, which is time-consuming and resource-intensive. AI and ML bring a data-driven paradigm to this complex landscape by enabling computational modeling, predictive analytics, and intelligent optimization of formulation parameters. These technologies can analyze multidimensional datasets to identify patterns and relationships between formulation components, physiological variables, and release kinetics that would be challenging to discern using traditional methods. AI-assisted models such as artificial neural networks, support vector machines, and Bayesian optimization have demonstrated significant potential in predicting drug release profiles, selecting optimal polymer systems, and simulating gastric behavior. Moreover, AI can streamline experimental design, reduce trial-anderror iterations, and accelerate the development timeline, thus improving formulation robustness and performance. The convergence of AI with gastroprotective systems also promises personalized approaches that account for patient-specific gastric motility and physiological factors, fostering tailored therapies. Although challenges remain—such as the need for high-quality datasets, interpretability of complex models, and integration with regulatory frameworks—the current advances provide a compelling foundation for future research. Embracing these intelligent tools in GRDDS development is likely to expand the frontiers of oral drug delivery by enhancing design precision, improving therapeutic outcomes, and reducing developmental costs. Continued innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration will be essential to fully harness the transformative potential of AI and ML in pharmaceutics.

Machine learning (ML), a subset of artificial intelligence (AI), is revolutionizing health care. Given the intricate anatomy and functional complexity of the hand, AI applications in hand pathology are gaining prominence, particularly in the diagnosis of fractures, nerve injuries, and musculoskeletal disorders. This review summarizes ML advancements in hand pathology diagnosis, enhancing clinical history analysis, examination findings interpretation, and imaging assessment. A systematic search of PubMed, Google Scholar, EMBASE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science from 1901 to March 2025 was conducted, focusing on ML applications in diagnosing hand fractures, tendon injuries, and nerve compressions. The inclusion criteria encompassed original research, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and observational studies that demonstrated the use of AI in diagnostic imaging, preoperative assessment, or postoperative management. Studies that did not involve AI-driven diagnostic applications or lacked sufficient methodological transparency were excluded. Machine learning models, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy in detecting fractures. Studies have validated CNNs in the detection of distal radius and ulna fractures, outperforming trainees and urgent care physicians. In addition, AI has enhanced clinical examination by integrating wearable motion sensors for objective joint assessment. However, challenges such as external validation, interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows remain, limiting broader clinical adoption. Machine learning shows promise in hand pathology diagnosis, but widespread adoption requires improved external validation, standardized methods, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Future research should prioritize multicentric studies and explainable AI to enhance trust and integration.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The rapid growth of urban populations and consumption patterns has significantly increased the volume and complexity of municipal waste streams, including recyclable, organic, hazardous, and electronic waste. Traditional waste management approaches such as manual sorting and fixed collection schedules struggle to handle the diversity and scale of modern waste systems efficiently. Consequently, recent research has explored artificial intelligence (AI), computer vision, and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies to automate waste classification and enable intelligent monitoring and management of waste infrastructures. However, the rapidly expanding literature in this domain is fragmented across different datasets, sensing platforms, and experimental settings, making it difficult to obtain a comprehensive understanding of current technological progress. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic literature review using the PRISMA methodology, analyzing 50 rigorously selected peer-reviewed studies on automated waste classification and intelligent waste management systems. The protocol was registered in the Open Science Framework (OSF). The reviewed works are examined in terms of model architectures, sensing infrastructures, datasets, and system capabilities. The analysis shows that convolutional neural network architectures such as ResNet, MobileNet, and EfficientNet, together with object detection frameworks including YOLO and Faster R-CNN, dominate current visual waste classification research; however, emerging studies increasingly explore hybrid architectures combining convolutional networks with transformer-based models to improve contextual understanding and scalability. IoT-enabled smart bins equipped with ultrasonic sensors, load cells, and environmental sensors are widely used for real-time waste monitoring. The review also reveals a recent surge of research activity, particularly in Asia, with increasing contributions from major publishers such as Elsevier and MDPI. Despite promising experimental performance, most systems remain limited to small curated datasets and pilot-scale deployments, highlighting a gap between laboratory research and real-world implementation. These findings provide a consolidated overview of current research trends and identify key challenges for developing scalable and practical intelligent waste management systems.

This study examines the symbolic meaning of PSHT martial arts movements from the plain belt to the green belt as nonverbal communication in members’ everyday lives. The study used a descriptive qualitative approach and symbolic interactionism, particularly Mead’s concepts of mind, self, and society. Data were obtained through in-depth interviews with five PSHT members, direct observation of training, documentation, and literature study. Data were analyzed through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings show that the movements are not understood merely as defensive techniques. They are interpreted as a progressive language of life: early movements emphasize confidence, awareness, and courage; subsequent movements emphasize self-control, situational awareness, and wise decision-making; later movements emphasize social responsibility and brotherhood. These meanings are internalized through repeated practice and interaction with trainers, elders, and members. Thus, PSHT movements function as embodied nonverbal symbols through which values are learned, interpreted, and enacted.
topics: Martial Arts: Techniques, Psychology, and Education

documents.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mechanical ventilators are essential life-support devices, yet evidence regarding device-related vulnerabilities remains limited compared with the extensive literature on human-factor-related adverse events. This study applied text-mining techniques to a large post-market surveillance database to examine ventilator malfunction reporting patterns and the effect of stratifying reports by device category. METHODS: Adverse event reports related to mechanical ventilators submitted to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience database between January 2010 and December 2025 were stratified into life-supporting and noninvasive devices and analyzed using KH Coder. A random sample of the life-supporting reports was drawn for the primary analysis. Frequency analysis, co-occurrence network analysis, hierarchical cluster analysis, and correspondence analysis were performed. Device brand and year were used as external variables in the correspondence analysis. RESULTS: A total of 193,926 reports met the eligibility criteria, of which 177,641 were classified as malfunctions. The analyses were restricted to reports classified as malfunctions. Among life-supporting ventilators, the reported malfunctions spanned several broad themes, including power and battery failures, circuit-board and electronic faults, breathing-circuit and gas-delivery problems, and issues involving monitoring and control functions. Among noninvasive devices, reports were concentrated in terms associated with a single foam-related recall, as well as connector corrosion and patient-reported symptoms. Nearly 1 in 5 malfunction reports did not document a confirmed device failure during patient use. CONCLUSIONS: Text mining of ventilator-related adverse event reports revealed distinct reporting patterns across life-supporting and noninvasive devices. These findings are exploratory and do not establish the frequency or causes of device failure. Stratification of reports by device category helped prevent the reporting patterns of individual devices from being obscured by a single recall. This study demonstrates the potential value of combining post-market surveillance data with text-mining methods to support medical device safety surveillance.

Artificial intelligence offers potential applications in wastewater monitoring, prediction, and operational decision support. However, selecting a model does not establish that factory managers and treatment operators can use it effectively. This conceptual article examines managerial readiness for artificial intelligence in Bangladesh's textile wastewater management. It brings together selected literature on organizational readiness, artificial intelligence capabilities, and wastewater applications, alongside Bangladesh-specific research and institutional reports. The article proposes six readiness domains: strategic commitment, managerial and operator knowledge, data stewardship, operational integration, investment and partnership capacity, and accountable decision making. It further distinguishes exploratory interest, supervised experimentation, routine decision support, and controlled operational integration as different adoption states. Four propositions explain how readiness may influence movement between these states and the translation of adoption into environmental performance. A proposed qualitative multiple-case design specifies evidence needed to examine these propositions, including decision histories, operational records, interviews across organizational levels, and observations of treatment routines. The framework is an analytical proposal rather than a validated measurement scale or report of completed fieldwork. Its contribution is to connect organizational preparation with the specific decisions, responsibilities, and verification practices required for textile wastewater management. Empirical research is needed to assess its relevance across factories with different resources and treatment arrangements.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Data-driven organizations increasingly depend on large, heterogeneous, and fast-moving data to sustain the quality of their products, services, and processes. The transition toward data-driven organizational quality, often discussed under the label of Quality 4.0, has so far been examined mainly through a managerial lens. As a result, the data foundations of that transition remain fragmented and under-theorized. This Conceptual Analysis reframes quality-oriented big data as a first-class data management problem and proposes a layered conceptual architecture that organizes the lifecycle of such data across five interconnected layers: multi-source acquisition, integration and fusion, data quality assurance, analytics and knowledge extraction, and data governance and ethics. The central argument is that data quality operates as a central mediating construct linking big data capability to organizational quality outcomes: analytics improves organizational quality in large part to the extent that the underlying data are accurate, complete, consistent, timely, and well governed. Drawing on the data management, data quality, and machine learning systems literatures, the article specifies the constituent elements of each layer, the dependencies among them, and the failure modes that arise when the data foundation is neglected. Five propositions and a structured research agenda position the acquisition, fusion, quality assurance, and governance of quality-oriented big data as priorities for data mining and management research. The architecture offers a data-centric vocabulary for designing and evaluating the data infrastructures on which data-driven organizational quality ultimately depends.

This study systematically maps and synthesizes the evolving literature on knowledge management (KM) in the context of Industry 4.0 (I4.0) by integrating bibliometric analysis with the Theory-Context-Characteristics-Method (TCCM) framework. Drawing on 93 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus (2018–2025), the study employs Biblioshiny and VOSviewer to analyze publication trends, intellectual structures, and thematic development, complemented by a structured TCCM-based synthesis. The findings reveal arapidly growing yet uneven field, dominated by perspectives on dynamic capabilities and absorptive capacity, with astrong concentration in manufacturing contexts and developed economies. Methodologically, the literature relies heavily on cross-sectional survey designs, while computational and longitudinal approaches remain limited. Thematic analysis identifies digital transformation, knowledge sharing, and organizational learning as core areas, whereas artificial intelligence, knowledge transfer, and governance remain underdeveloped. To address these gaps, the study proposes the Dynamic Knowledge Management Capability (DKMC) framework, conceptualizing KM as a technology-mediated capability shaped by human-AI interaction, real-time knowledge flows, and governance mechanisms. The study provides a transparent, theory-integrated synthesis and contributes to KM scholarship by incorporating AI-mediated knowledge processes and governance considerations, offering directions for future research and practice in digitally intensive environments.

The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and lifelong learning has attracted growing educational, computational, and policy attention, yet its intellectual structure has not been mapped systematically. This study reports a scientometric analysis of the AI-lifelong learning literature indexed in Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection between 2014 and 2024. Records retrieved from both databases (N = 347) were merged and duplicated in ScientoPy, yielding 259 unique documents. Research momentum was quantified with three time-normalized indicators, average growth rate (AGR), average documents per year (ADY), and percentage of documents published in the last years (PDLY), across six analytical dimensions. Output grew from one document in 2014 to 116 in 2024; across the five principal document types (n = 220), 70.5% of records appeared in 2023-2024. Conference papers (41.3%) and journal articles (38.2%) predominated, with articles expanding fastest (AGR = 21.5; PDLY = 71.7%). Education & Educational Research recorded the highest normalized momentum among subject categories (AGR = 7.0; PDLY = 89.5%). Lifelong learning (n = 57) and artificial intelligence (n = 53) anchored the keyword field, while ChatGPT and Higher Education emerged entirely within the final two years. The United States led in volume (n = 57), whereas India (n = 29; PDLY = 89.7%) showed the strongest recent acceleration. Triangulating these indicators suggests, as an interpretive inference rather than a network-based measurement, that the corpus comprises three largely separate epistemic communities sharing a label but not a research program, framing an agenda for integrative, ethically grounded scholarship.
topics: Diverse Approaches in Healthcare and Education Studies

documents.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) remain unreliable for extremely low-resource languages whose writing systems conflict with high-resource pretraining priors. We study Bai-Chinese translation in the Bowen script, where Chinese characters are frequently borrowed phonetically rather than semantically, causing severe literal-translation hallucinations. We propose MAS-Bai, a linguistically informed adaptive multi-agent framework for Bowen-script Bai-Chinese translation. MAS-Bai routes each input through either a lightweight retrieval-translation path or a deeper philological path with etymological and syntactic agents, and uses cycle-consistency with a lightweight reverse translator as an inference-time reliability signal. We construct a 6,536-sentence Bai-Chinese corpus and evaluate on a 1,536-sentence test set. MAS-Bai achieves 16.23 BLEU and 62.15 COMET, improving over Standard RAG by 8.11 BLEU and 6.85 COMET. Forward LoRA, expert ablations and controlled routing experiments distinguish the roles of supervised adaptation, Bai-specific expertise and conditional routing. The largest gains occur on Bowen phonetic loans and divergent Bai word order, while human evaluation and reverse-verifier analyses support the automatic results.

Measuring organizational constructs in large-scale unstructured text requires methods that preserve interpretive depth while enabling systematic, per-document classification. Structural Topic Modeling (STM) supports interpretive depth by surfacing patterns that inform construct operationalization, but its topic proportions are not designed as standalone per-document construct measures; transformer-based models such as BERT can scale measurement but require construct operationalization grounded in interpretive work. We address this challenge through a two-stage framework in which STM and BERT play structurally distinct roles. Coding schemes are developed through qualitative interpretation and STM analysis; BERT is then fine-tuned to apply these schemes across documents. We formalize two research approaches—construct-guided and pattern-discovery—that provide principled paths from different theoretical starting points toward a shared methodological endpoint: validated, auditable per-document construct measures. We illustrate the framework using more than 20,000 employee reviews. The framework supports iterative construct validation, using computational diagnostics to guide interpretive refinement and producing document-level measures suitable for theory-informed organizational analysis.

Global shipping carries over 80% of world trade, yet existing supply-chain-resilience theory models resilience at the level of the firm, node and network, without treating the workforce operating those nodes as a variable. This study addresses that gap using the 2023–2026 Red Sea/Houthi crisis as its empirical setting. A mixed-methods, pilot-scale design combined a 64-respondent self-report questionnaire of serving seafarers with thematic analysis of open-text responses. Seafarers exposed to Red Sea transits, Cape of Good Hope diversions, or a security incident rated STCW crisis-management training as significantly less adequate for conflict-area risk than unexposed seafarers, an effect that strengthened for incident-exposed respondents specifically. Open-text responses identified situational information and realistic scenario-based drills, rather than generic compliance training, as the specific gap, and a minority questioned seafarers' right to decline a high-risk voyage. These findings extend the conceptual framework linking geopolitical risk to operational resilience by distinguishing a training-competence pathway from a retention/psychological-contract pathway. The study contributes empirical evidence, gathered directly from an affected workforce, that the human factor is a measurable variable in geopolitical supply-chain-disruption theory, and derives practical and policy recommendations for STCW training content and seafarer consent protections.
topics: Supply Chain Resilience and Risk Management

documents.abstract: Background: Metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUH-NW) describes individuals with a body mass index (BMI) within the normal range who nevertheless present cardiometabolic abnormalities. Evidence regarding this phenotype in specific female occupational populations remains limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of MUH-NW among female domestic workers and to characterize its associated anthropometric, clinical, biochemical, and lifestyle factors. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted using occupational health surveillance data from female domestic workers in Spain. The analysis included 3,344 women with a BMI of 18.5–24.9 kg/m². MUH-NW was defined as the presence of at least two of four abnormalities: elevated blood pressure (≥130/85 mmHg), fasting glucose ≥100 mg/dL, triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL, and HDL-cholesterol Results: MUH-NW was identified in 352 women (10.5%; 95% CI, 9.5–11.6%), while 41.1% presented at least one metabolic abnormality. Low HDL-cholesterol (26.8%) and elevated blood pressure (18.2%) were the most frequent abnormalities. MUH-NW was associated with age (OR per year 1.13; 95% CI, 1.11–1.15), current smoking (OR 1.71; 95% CI, 1.31–2.22), and physical inactivity (OR 3.23; 95% CI, 2.21–4.71). Lack of Mediterranean diet adherence was not independently associated with MUH-NW after adjustment. Among anthropometric indices, BAI showed the strongest adjusted association (OR per SD 1.51; 95% CI, 1.32–1.73). However, individual anthropometric measures showed only modest discrimination. BAI had the highest AUC (0.680), but its performance was not significantly different from BMI (AUC 0.660; ΔAUC=0.021; DeLong p=0.164). Conclusions: Cardiometabolic abnormalities were present in a substantial proportion of normal-weight female domestic workers. MUH-NW was cross-sectionally associated with older age, current smoking, physical inactivity, and selected anthropometric measures. However, anthropometric indices alone showed limited ability to discriminate metabolic health status. These findings indicate that normal BMI does not necessarily coincide with a favorable cardiometabolic profile and support consideration of metabolic information alongside BMI when characterizing cardiometabolic health in normal-weight women. Given the cross-sectional design, the observed associations should not be interpreted as causal relationships.

Supervised fine-tuning on agent trajectories is an effective way to improve coding agents, but selecting useful training examples requires more than identifying successful runs. A resolved patch may follow inefficient reasoning or unnecessary tool use, while a failed run may still contain useful intermediate steps. Training pipelines therefore rely on rules and qualitative assessments to filter trajectories, yet designing these filters typically requires substantial human expertise, and validating improvements through repeated training and evaluation is expensive. We introduce MetaCurate, a training-free framework that evolves executable trajectory curation filters using pairwise LLM judgments. Disagreements between the filter's rankings and the judge's preferences provide targeted feedback for jointly revising its rules, rubric, and aggregation policy. The resulting filter scores trajectories independently, so pairwise comparisons are required only during search. Starting from a blank filter, MetaCurate autonomously discovers a curation strategy that achieves competitive downstream performance without task-specific handwritten criteria. We validate downstream utility through controlled SFT experiments on our uncurated trajectory pool and the Nemotron v3 SWE dataset, with random selection and hand-authored filtering as baselines. In our experiments, MetaCurate achieves the highest mean SWE-Verified score among the compared methods, including hand-authored rule-based filtering and a training-loop baseline whose search costs 3.5x as much.

topics: Innovative Microfluidic and Catalytic Techniques Innovation

documents.abstract: The increasing demand for renewable energy and the urgent need to mitigate climate change have driven global interest in bioethanol as a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels. However, reliance on edible feedstocks such as corn, sugarcane or wheat has proven unsustainable due to food-fuel competition. In contrast, second-generation bioethanol production that utilizes lignocellulosic biomass primarily depends on a single biomass, limiting the continuous production because of seasonal variability and high production costs. Mixed lignocellulosic biomass (MLB) utilization has emerged as a promising strategy to address these challenges by integrating diverse agricultural residues, forestry waste, energy crops and industrial by-products within biorefineries. MLB provides supply stability, enhances enzymatic saccharification and minimizes inhibitor formation through synergistic buffering and compositional complementarity. This review comprehensively evaluates the significance of feedstock diversity, pretreatment strategies, enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation approaches in MLB-based bioethanol production. It further examines process integration strategies, such as simultaneous saccharification and fermentation, consolidated bioprocessing and hybrid reactor systems for year-round operations. Techno-economic assessments demonstrate that MLB reduces the production costs, while life-cycle analyses confirm significant greenhouse gas mitigation potential. Despite these advantages, this study describes challenges in feedstock logistics, inhibitor management, strain robustness and process stability. Moreover, it outlines future directions that emphasize the roles of artificial intelligence and machine learning in feedstock blending, synthetic biology for robust microbial consortia and supportive policy frameworks to promote biomass aggregation. Overall, MLB represents a scalable and sustainable pathway for continuous second-generation bioethanol production, offering environmental, economic and technological advantages over single-feed approaches.

AI agents are increasingly expected to modify and maintain machine-learning systems in production, yet existing benchmarks primarily evaluate either competition-style ML experimentation or generic repository issue resolution. We introduce MLOps-Bench, a repository-grounded benchmark for production ML engineering. Unlike prior ML-agent benchmarks, MLOps-Bench evaluates executable lifecycle changes inside real ML repositories, spanning data pipelines, feature engineering, model training, model serving, monitoring, CI/CD and governance, and end-to-end integration. Each task is grounded in repository evidence and includes a natural-language requirement, oracle patch, plausible buggy baseline, fail-to-pass tests, pass-to-pass tests, and provenance metadata. The benchmark contains 212 validated tasks from 31 public ML repositories, with 636 fail-to-pass tests and 856 pass-to-pass tests. We evaluate six agents and find that the best system solves 31.2% of tasks while passing 68.7% of tests, showing that current agents often make partial progress but still fail production-relevant behavioral requirements. MLOps-Bench shifts agent evaluation beyond model building and issue fixing toward repository-native MLOps work where correctness depends on lifecycle reasoning, behavioral robustness, and preservation of existing system behavior.

Multimodal large language model (MLLM)-based mobile agents are rapidly evolving from conversational assistants into autonomous systems that perceive, reason over, and act on smartphone environments. This capability also exposes a new security risk: adversaries can embed malicious objectives in cross-application mobile content and steer agent behavior through indirect multimodal injection. Although prompt injection has been studied in desktop and web settings, its cross-modal properties in mobile ecosystems remain poorly understood, and existing security analyses are still limited. To close this gap, we introduce MobileInject, the first benchmark for evaluating mobile agents against multimodal injection attacks and reasoning-to-action security risks. MobileInject provides a high-fidelity interactive mobile evaluation framework covering 11 scenarios, 9 security-risk categories, and 108 executable risk instances. It further introduces Cross-Modal Consistency Injection to exploit corroboration across modalities, two enhanced attack methods, Multi-Role Collaborative Deception and Reasoning-Camouflage Injection, to intensify trust manipulation and reasoning hijacking, and a Reasoning Security Diagnosis Framework for fine-grained failure analysis. Systematic experiments show that mobile agents are broadly vulnerable to multimodal injection, and that many failures stem from reasoning hijacking at early stages. These findings establish MobileInject as a systematic cross-modal benchmark for studying and improving the security of mobile agents. Code release details are provided in the Appendix Open Science section.

Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly incorporated into agent-based models (ABMs) on the premise that richer, context-sensitive human behavior can improve empirical fidelity. However, LLM-supported ABMs introduce an open-ended design space in which subtle modeling and configuration choices, such as prompt design and environment coupling, can substantially alter outcomes. Developing LLM-supported ABMs to simulate human collective behavior therefore requires navigating configuration sensitivity while identifying the limitations of the current model architecture. In this paper, we introduce the \textit{Model Capacity Frontier} (MCF), a framework that characterizes the empirical performance attainable by a specified architecture across its admissible configurations. In multi-objective settings, this capacity is represented by an estimated Pareto frontier obtained through systematic configuration exploration. We demonstrate MCF in crowd simulation of university commencement events with approximately 12,000 agents, using empirical movement data on temporal occupancy, spatial distribution, and flow direction. We first characterize the capacity of a conventional crowd model and then evaluate successive LLM-supported architectural extensions. In the process, MCF reveals which dimensions of attainable performance expand and which remain limited, providing empirical targets for refinement and re-evaluation. Initial LLM integration improves flow direction but degrades temporal occupancy and spatial distribution; subsequent architectural refinement of the LLM layer improves temporal occupancy and recovers spatial performance, while retaining much of the earlier gain in flow direction. Our case study shows how MCF guides the systematic architectural development of LLM-supported ABMs in configuration-sensitive, open-ended design spaces.

Historical pre-crash scenarios contain a sequence of vehicle-to-vehicle interactions, among which the critical pre-crash interaction is the one that most directly leads to the eventual collision. Identifying such critical interactions is important for uncovering potential safety risks in Autonomous Driving Systems (ADSs). However, this task remains challenging because the critical interaction is often embedded within numerous preceding interactions and needs to be distinguished by considering how the pre-crash scenario evolves over time. To address this challenge, we propose MICA, a model-based multi-agent approach for identifying critical pre-crash interactions from textual accident reports. Unlike existing LLM-based approaches that directly identify critical interactions from accident reports, MICA explicitly models the evolution of pre-crash interactions through multi-agent collaboration. Specialized LLM-based agents extract and validate relevant information to construct a Pre-crash Evolution Model, from which the critical interaction is identified by matching the modeled interactions to predefined pre-crash patterns. We evaluate MICA on 200 accident reports released by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV CA). The results demonstrate that MICA effectively identifies critical pre-crash interactions across different accident report data sources, scenario complexities, and underlying LLMs.

The objective of this study was to use artificial intelligence (AI) to predict mastery-approach goals in secondary school students based on variables from the PISA 2018 database. The sample consisted of 339,560 participants from 60 countries. Machine learning was used with the Super Learner mega-algorithm with 14 candidate algorithms. In addition, deep learning was used with a neural network with 107 parameters. The analyses showed that students’ perceived parental emotional support, competitiveness, purpose in life, self-efficacy, and knowledge of intercultural communication were predictors of mastery-approach goals in secondary school students. This research contributes to the study of factors that influence mastery-approach goals in secondary school students, with analysis models that advance the development of the science of AI-based predictive education.

Modern LLM applications rely on runtime monitors that inspect tool calls, traces, streams, detector outputs, and verifier inputs. This creates an interface-reliability problem: a framework path may remain operational while policy-relevant evidence never reaches its decision point. In one representative case, a regex detector returned a positive match, but the framework stranded the result before the block decision. This differs from jailbreaks and detector errors because the evidence is already recognized yet disconnected from enforcement. We study this repair-boundary signature with canary contracts: parent/fixed confirmation units that place a known payload only on the changed evidence surface and record monitor visibility together with the downstream decision for action-boundary cases. Applying the protocol to public framework repairs, we confirm 18 evidence-path failures across 11 LLM or agent safety project groups and four implementation ecosystems. Nine are established-boundary repairs, eight are new-surface policy-coverage gaps, and one is a boundary-only evidence case. Fourteen reach E1 enforcement boundaries: seven native action outcomes, six configured enforcement boundaries, and one synthetic-consumer consequence. The remaining cases affect verifier, safety-prompt, or observability channels. The cases form carrier, adapter, authority, and surface families and show how ordinary application behavior can remain intact while a safety-specific evidence path misses its decision. Exact revisions, deterministic outcomes, negative controls, and a frozen prospective audit document the confirmation rule. Monitor assumptions therefore need regression tests at the schemas, streams, tools, and adapters that frameworks evolve.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Multi-turn image editing aims to modify an image according to a sequence of instructions, making it better aligned with human-AI collaborative creation than single-turn editing. However, constructing high-quality multi-turn training data remains challenging, as conventional sequential rollout accumulates errors and introduces visual-quality drift across editing turns. To address this challenge, we introduce MTEdit, a multi-turn image editing dataset built through a pipeline centered on packed trajectory canvas (PTC) generation. By jointly generating multiple editing states within a unified visual context, this pipeline reduces visual-quality drift across turns. Covering both step-wise and context-aware editing scenarios, MTEdit comprises 500K multi-turn image editing trajectories, with up to 8 turns and an average of 5.38 turns per trajectory, making it one of the most extensive datasets for multi-turn image editing. We further introduce MTEdit-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate both scenarios by assessing models' ability to follow editing instructions, maintain content consistency, resist visual-quality drift, and effectively use historical context across turns. Using MTEdit, we fine-tune Qwen-Image-Edit-Causal to obtain Qwen-Image-MTEdit. On MTEdit-Bench, we evaluate a broad range of closed-source and open-source image editing models, including Qwen-Image-MTEdit. Experimental results show that Qwen-Image-MTEdit achieves the best performance among the evaluated open-source models, demonstrating the effectiveness of MTEdit in improving models' multi-turn image editing capabilities.
topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

documents.abstract: We investigate the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in multi-author style change detection. Using off-the-shelf LLMs or supervised fine-tuning solely within the target domain fails to yield effective features; for this reason, we propose cross-domain transfer learning with LLM-based embeddings fine-tuned for authorship verification. We fine-tune Mistral-7B embedding model and compare it with DeBERTa, used in the state-of-the-art (SOTA) systems in PAN-25 multi-author writing style analysis challenge. Results show that DeBERTa and Mistral excel in different user-generated text scenarios. We exploit this diversity by combining both embeddings, leading to more effective style change detection.

The construction industry faces growing challenges that require better decision-making frameworks. Combining Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) with digital tools like Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a promising way forward. Yet their integration remains fragmented across research efforts, revealing a significant gap in theory and practice. As a result, their potential remains underutilized, limiting the development of flexible, data-driven decision-making tools for complex construction projects. This study conducts a systematic bibliometric analysis to map the development and structure of the MCDM-BIM-AI connection in construction management from 2015 to 2025. Using a PRISMA-compliant protocol, we analyzed 253 peer-reviewed articles from the Scopus database. Our approach combines performance analysis with science mapping through keyword co-occurrence networks and thematic evolution analysis across three time periods: 2015-2018, 2019-2021, 2022-2025, along with a country-level co-authorship network analysis. Our findings identify five main thematic clusters and show a significant increase in publications since 2019, mainly driven by the Asia-Pacific region. The analysis highlights a notable knowledge gap in the deep connection between BIM and AI within MCDM frameworks. The temporal mapping reveals three phases of evolution: pre-integration (2015-2018), Integration (2019-2021), and Innovation (2022-present), with AI and Machine Learning becoming key focus areas in the latest phase. The study suggests promising future directions for combining MCDM, BIM, and AI to promote more sustainable, data-driven, and resilient construction practices. It proposes a conceptual outline for the Intelligent Cognitive Decision Framework (ICDF), where BIM serves as a semantic data backbone, MCDM acts as the evaluation engine, and AI provides cognitive support for flexible, data-driven decision-making in construction 4.0 applications. This intellectual mapping offers researchers data-driven guidance for prioritizing impactful investigations, practitioners with technology investment plans that match research developments, and policymakers with informed priorities for research and development investment in underrepresented regions.

In a hierarchical multi-agent system, a Leader assigns tasks and subagents carry them out. Jointly training the Leader and the subagents is difficult because a final answer gives only indirect feedback to the subagents. An LLM judge can score the performance of the subagents, but these scores depend on the judge's own assessment of the quality of subagents' responses. We present MultiAgent-OPD, which combines on-policy distillation with reinforcement learning to jointly train a shared-parameter Leader-Searcher-Answerer team end to end. We first train a Teacher in a Searcher-Answerer workflow using answer correctness. During team training, the frozen Teacher scores student-generated search and summary tokens to provide local process supervision for the Searchers, while the Leader learns from team success and the Answerer from candidate correctness. Across seven datasets, the trained system reaches 38.68% macro avg@4, exceeding Prompted Critic by 4.06 percentage points and C-MAS + RL, the trained cascaded multiagent system, by 2.61 percentage points. The team also solves more questions within four attempts.

The reuse of open government works on the web has increased rapidly with the expansion of public data policies and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted content utilization. In Korea, Korea Open Government Licenses (KOGLs) permit the reuse of public works under conditions such as attribution, non-commercial use, and no-derivatives. However, these conditions are frequently violated or misunderstood in web pages, advertisements, social media posts, and reused digital content. Since compliance-related evidence is distributed across textual descriptions, captions, license metadata, embedded image text, visual changes, and page-level context, manual inspection, and single-modal analysis are not sufficient for scalable web-based compliance review. This paper proposes a multimodal evidence-based method for KOGL license compliance risk prediction in web environments. The proposed method combines textual context, KOGL metadata, optical character recognition (OCR) extracted image text, and visual features to classify four risk types: attribution risk, non-commercial use risk, no-derivatives risk, and false KOGL claim risk. A lightweight sequential context model captures the contextual flow of compliance-related cues, while the decision module produces both risk probabilities and evidence-based explanations. Experiments on a KOGL-oriented dataset show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy, macro-F1, and area under the curve (AUC) than text-only, image-only, and simple fusion baselines. The results demonstrate that multimodal web evidence improves compliance risk prediction and provides practical support for human review in public content management, open government data curation, and AI training data inspection.

Multi-turn jailbreaks use feedback from a victim large language model to adapt their queries over several turns. However, once an effective trajectory has been found, it is unclear how much of the earlier query history is still needed. In this work, we study this by removing early attacker queries and running the remaining queries again in a new conversation while regenerating the victim's responses. We define the effective horizon as the shortest remaining query sequence that recovers the same attack progress. Empirically, we find that roughly half of the original query sequence is sufficient on average to recover the same attack progress. We call this phenomenon effective-horizon compression. We show that this shorter history can recover the best point reached during an unsuccessful attack and provide a better starting point for continuing the attack. It also helps identify which earlier queries should receive less learning signal during attacker training, and downweighting those queries improves performance. We further find that short reward-propagation windows preserve calibrated defense performance close to full-trajectory returns. These results show that multi-turn attacks can contain more queries than are needed to recover the progress reached later in the interaction.

This study aimed to assess musculoskeletal and ergonomic risk, identify demographic, occupational, lifestyle, and biomechanical characteristics associated with these outcomes, and develop and prioritize ergonomic intervention strategies for petrochemical control room operators. This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 among 210 male control room operators from an Iranian petrochemical complex using census sampling. Data were collected using the Demographic/Occupational Questionnaire, Persian International Physical Activity Questionnaire (P-IPAQ), Persian Örebro Musculoskeletal Pain Screening Questionnaire (P-ÖMSQ), and Persian Ergonomic Screening and Priority Tool (P-ESPT), complemented by objective postural and plantar pressure assessments. The P-ÖMSQ was used to classify participants according to P-ÖMSQ risk categories, with scores ≥ 90 categorized as moderate-to-high risk. Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software, version 20.0, with descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression. A P-ÖMSQ score within the moderate-to-high risk categories (≥ 90) was observed in 27% of participants, while 78% were classified as having moderate-to-high ergonomic risk. Multivariable logistic regression showed that older age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.09, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.02–1.17, p = 0.014), higher body mass index (BMI) (aOR = 1.15, 95% CI = 1.04–1.27, p = 0.006), and longer job tenure (aOR = 1.98, 95% CI = 1.01–3.89, p = 0.047) were independently associated with higher odds of being classified in the moderate-to-high-risk P-ÖMSQ category. Lower physical activity was significantly associated with a higher prevalence of forward head posture, thoracic hyperkyphosis, lateral pelvic tilt, and pes planus ( p < 0.05). Objective biomechanical abnormalities were also significantly associated with higher P-ÖMSQ-based and P-ESPT-based risk categories ( p < 0.05). Based on the study findings, 20 ergonomic intervention strategies were proposed and prioritized through a stakeholder-informed participatory process. Older age, higher body mass index, and longer job tenure were associated with higher odds of being classified in the moderate-to-high-risk P-ÖMSQ category, while lower physical activity was associated with selected postural abnormalities among petrochemical control room operators. Several objective biomechanical abnormalities were also associated with P-ÖMSQ-based and P-ESPT-based risk categories. These findings may inform the prioritization of workplace ergonomic interventions; however, the proposed interventions were not evaluated in the present study, and their effectiveness should be assessed in future longitudinal and interventional studies.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Colleges record semester results in spreadsheets, and answering even a simple question about them, such as how one section performed compared with another, usually means filtering and calculating by hand or writing SQL. This paper presents the Natural Language Database Query and Analytics Agent, a system that lets non-technical users ask such questions in plain English. The agent supplies the schema of a relational database to a large language model, which writes a SQL query. The query is checked, executed in read-only mode, corrected using the database error message if it fails, and the result is returned as text, a table or a chart. The design is applied to the Information Science and Engineering result sheets of 206 students over three semesters (IV, V and VI). Example questions are run against the prepared database, and their answers are reported as ground truth for future testing, along with data-quality problems found in the source sheets. The measured accuracy of the model-generated queries is left for future work.

By automating the content creation process, Generative AI is reshaping creative work, but its impact on knowledge workers remains underexplored, which this study seeks to examine. Drawing on in-depth interviews with 20 knowledge workers, this study examines what is being transformed in the workplace and how these shifts are being perceived by the knowledge workers who use GenAI. Using Social Shaping of Technology (SST) as a conceptual lens to understand the interaction between technology and knowledge workers, the study finds that participants perceived GenAI as an efficient tool that provides cognitive relief and enhances productivity during times of resource constraint. Tensions also arose around authenticity, creativity, a sense of fulfillment, and the perception of effort. The adoption of GenAI has created downstream labor and demand for new skills as it shifts knowledge workers’ roles away from creator to editor/fact-checker while creating tension as participants balance their desire for efficiency with fears of diminished creativity and domain knowledge, skills atrophy, and threats to content ownership.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: This chapter addresses the rapid integration of AI technology, especially Gen AI, into our lives and especially the teaching and learning practices in higher education, foregrounding a range of unresolved social, ecological and academic issues this entails. A ninth capability is proposed as necessary for flourishing in this complex technology-infused age. The chapter also discusses the linkages between inquiry, integrity, learning, and Artificial Intelligence.
