documents.abstract: To explore the key factors affecting the vertical collaboration of county and township medical personnel within county-level medical alliances and the paths for improvement, in order to provide suggestions for enhancing the intrinsic motivation for collaboration among county and township medical personnel. Based on D’Amour’s organizational collaboration theory, the CLFI vertical collaboration theoretical framework was constructed. Following this framework, a questionnaire was designed and administered using random sampling within one county-level medical alliance in Fujian Province, achieving a valid response rate of 96.95%. Ten dimensions, including shared goals and patient-centered orientation, were regarded as antecedent conditions. Fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis was employed to extract the pathways for enhancing the vertical collaboration capacity of county and township medical personnel. There are eight different configuration combinations, which can be summarized into five capability enhancement paths, namely the policy-driven path, the functional synergy path, the service-oriented path, the innovation-driven path, and the relationship-building path. The consistency of the solutions for these five combinations of causal conditions reached 82.2%. Strategically, policy coordination should be strengthened; cognitive linkages should be enhanced; patient outcomes should be embedded throughout the processes of collaborative goal setting, process design, and performance evaluation; a tolerance and assessment mechanism should be established to provide pilot support and dynamic monitoring for collaborative innovation; mutual trust among county and township medical personnel should be solidified, along with the consolidation of professional division of labor and capacity support, to promote the medical community’s transition from spontaneous cooperation to conscious coordination, ultimately achieving improved quality and efficiency in primary healthcare service capabilities. Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the teaching and working aspects in institutions of higher learning, but there is a lack of empirical knowledge on the economic preparedness and sustainability perception of the stakeholders. Most of the previous studies on educational technology adoption are based on behavioral intention and technological acceptance, though the economic sustainability (such as perceived economic value and affordability) is under-researched, especially in developing economies like India (Aaradhi and Chakraborty, 2024; Feng et al. , 2025). The research question of this paper is how the willingness to continue involvement with AI driven learning systems is determined by economic perceptions (value and affordability), financial access, and technological properties. Five universities in central India were sampled (412 students and faculty) and data were collected and then analyzed through Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). Findings indicate that perceived economic value and affordability affect the sustainability readiness in a positive way, and technological features enhance confidence in the long-term engagement. The results have a policy, university budgeting, and EdTech development strategies implication towards sustainable AI adoption.

Concerns about generative AI in medical training often focus on eroded reasoning and deskilling. Such competence-based accounts are incomplete. We identify a neglected casualty: critical-feedback tolerance (CFT), the capacity to receive disconfirming evaluative feedback and remain productively engaged. Affirmation-optimized systems may lower CFT undetectably, surfacing only under authentic critique. This conceptual Perspective defines CFT, differentiates it from six established constructs, specifies measurable facets, and states explicit refutation conditions.

documents.abstract: ABSTRACT Trajectory captioning aims to represent trajectories in natural language texts, providing a human‐friendly approach to understanding and utilizing trajectory data. Previous trajectory captioning methods relied on manually defined rule templates to describe trajectories, failing to accurately and comprehensively capture the trajectory semantics. To address these issues, this paper synthesizes the semantics of the origin and destination (OD) points of trajectories with large language models (LLMs) to improve trajectory captioning. The proposed method first designs a trajectory context augmentation module that enriches the trajectories' context using the spatial information from Point‐of‐Interest (POI) distributions and human travel data from check‐in records. The method develops a geographical semantic‐based reasoning module that constructs a time‐subcategory graph and trains a POI matching module to capture the geographical semantics of the trajectories. Finally, a trajectory decoding module is developed, which leverages LLMs and the Chain‐of‐Thought inspired strategies to generate trajectory captions. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method outperforms baseline methods on both lexical‐overlap and semantic‐alignment metrics. This paper explores a new approach for trajectory semantics representation and provides a methodological reference for the text generation tasks in various geographical applications.

The ability to selectively eliminate pathogenic proteins rather than merely inhibit their activity has redefined contemporary drug discovery, positioning targeted protein degradation (TPD) as one of the most significant advances in chemical biology and precision therapeutics.By harnessing endogenous protein quality-control machinery, TPD offers a catalytic and event-driven pharmacological strategy capable of addressing limitations associated with conventional occupancydriven inhibitors, including poor target selectivity, transient target engagement, acquired resistance, and the inaccessibility of many disease-relevant proteins.Among the expanding repertoire of degrader technologies, proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) and molecular glues have emerged as the most mature and clinically advanced platforms, each employing distinct mechanisms to recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases and direct selective protein degradation.Their rapid evolution has been driven by breakthroughs in structural biology, medicinal chemistry, computational modeling, and artificial intelligence, enabling the rational design of degraders with enhanced potency, selectivity, and pharmacokinetic performance.Beyond oncology, these technologies are increasingly being explored for neurological, inflammatory, infectious, and rare genetic disorders, underscoring their broad therapeutic potential.Nevertheless, challenges related to E3 ligase diversity, tissue specificity, resistance mechanisms, safety, and clinical translation continue to influence their successful implementation.This review critically examines the molecular foundations, design principles, therapeutic applications, and clinical progress of PROTACs and molecular glues while integrating emerging targeted degradation platforms and technological innovations.Furthermore, it discusses the opportunities and unresolved challenges that will shape the next generation of degrader therapeutics and their transformative role in the future of precision drug discovery.

Abstract We introduce TD-Interpreter, a specialised machine learning (ML) workflow that assists engineers in understanding complex timing diagrams (TDs), originating from a third party, during their design and verification process. The outcome of this workflow is a visual question-answer environment which allows engineers to input a set of TDs and ask design and verification queries regarding these TDs. To address limited training data availability, we developed a synthetic data generation pipeline that aligns visual information with its textual interpretation. We then implemented TD-Interpreter using a lightweight 7B Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM), guided by both supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL). We also developed extensive TD-reasoning benchmarks from simple retrieval tasks to complex reasoning problems in the real world. Our experimental results show that TD-Interpreter substantially outperformed both the untuned base model, and commercial MLLMs (GPT-5.2), on the evaluated benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed workflow.

Mental illnesses are on the rise all over the world and there is a need to detect depression through digital footprints in an automated and early manner.The traditional Artificial Intelligence (AI) paradigms do not usually have context-based and user behavioral information.To overcome these shortcomings, this research paper suggested the Transformer-Based Depression Detection Network (TDD-Net) that combined textual information with user-centric behavioral metadata built on a fully primary and consented social media dataset.The data included self-written posts, captions, comments, patterns of interactions and anonymized profile data.Text cleaning, sentiment normalization and tokenization were done by using a systematic preprocessing pipeline.A RoBERTa encoder was used to learn the semantic representation of text, and a metadata embedding network was used to learn longitudinal behavioral signals, including posting frequency, intensity of engagement, and diurnal activity patterns.The linguistic and metadata vectors were fused with a fusion layer and a multi-head attention classification head was applied to predict the risk of depression.This transformer fusion, which is metadata-enhanced, boosted personalization in depression detection.An experimental assessment revealed an accuracy of 97.18, and better precision, recall, and F1-scores.These findings show that the model has high predictive accuracy, and it is used in practice in mental health monitoring.TDD-Net is a big improvement over the conventional text-only approach by making good use of extensive behavioral cues.
